purpose: An empirical relation (proposed by Singh et al.) to calculate the increase in dislocation density of the material with the imposed equivalent plastic strain during constrained grooves pressing/warm working conditions, used here to estimate the dislocation density after multiaxial forging (MAF).
applicability_conditions: Empirical relation originally proposed by Singh et al. [41] for constrained grooves pressing at warm conditions, with constants obtained from cold rolling data [42,43]; in this study it is applied to low-density Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8 C steel (predominantly austenite phase) that has undergone MAF passes, where ρ0 is the dislocation density of MAF-0 and the material strengthening prediction is valid up to a small/medium number of MAF passes (low-strain cold working).

symbols.meaning: Dislocation density after deformation (final dislocation density)
Dislocation density of the initial material (dislocation density of MAF-0 in the present investigation)
Constant obtained from non-linear curve fit of experimental dislocation density vs imposed strain (accounts for the maximum attainable dislocation density increment)
Constant obtained from the non-linear curve fit of experimental dislocation density and imposed strain (rate/saturation parameter describing how rapidly the increment develops with strain)

unmapped: The relation was originally proposed by Singh et al. [41]; constants k1 and k2 were derived from non-linear curve fitting for cold rolling in [42,43].
In the present investigation, k1 and k2 are obtained by curve fitting of dislocation density vs imposed equivalent strain using data from Table 1 and Fig. 6.
The equation is implemented in a VUMAT subroutine along with Eq. (8) for FE simulation of dislocation generation and grain size evolution during MAF.
Dislocation density is estimated from XRD analysis through lattice microstrain via the Williamson-Hall plot, with Burgers vector b = 0.259 nm.
With increasing plastic strain, dislocation density first increases to a maximum and then the increment decreases; dislocations rearrange at a critical strain of 2.3 (five MAF passes).
